summary: Shows add_host examples: adding a host to a group with a variable, to multiple groups, with a non-standard port, as a tunnel alias via `ansible_host`/`ansible_port` (or `ansible_ssh_*` on 1.9 and older), restoring `inventory_dir`, and adding all play hosts to a group in a loop.
questions: How do I add a host to multiple groups with add_host?
How do I add a host I reach through an SSH tunnel?
How do I put every host that ran the playbook into a group?
How do I set a host variable when adding a host?

answer_card.title: add_host examples
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.add_host:
    name: '{{ ip_from_ec2 }}'
    groups: just_created
    foo: 42                      # host var

- ansible.builtin.add_host:
    hostname: '{{ new_ip }}'
    groups: [group1, group2]

- ansible.builtin.add_host:
    name: '{{ new_ip }}:{{ new_port }}'   # non-standard port

- ansible.builtin.add_host:         # tunnel alias, Ansible 2.0+
    hostname: '{{ new_ip }}'
    ansible_host: '{{ inventory_hostname }}'
    ansible_port: '{{ new_port }}'

- ansible.builtin.add_host:         # close to pre-2.4 inventory_dir behavior
    hostname: charlie
    inventory_dir: '{{ inventory_dir }}'

- ansible.builtin.add_host:
    name: '{{ item }}'
    groups: done
  loop: "{{ ansible_play_hosts }}"
```
(On 1.9 and older, use `ansible_ssh_host`/`ansible_ssh_port`.)
